rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.e1: With the pawn on d2, the key squares are c4, d4 and e4. The black king, on f5, is already next to e4, and yours, on a6, is further from them.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.e4: The opposition also works along a rank: that is lateral opposition. The count is the same: an odd number of squares between the kings after your move, with your king on the way to the key squares.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.p: White to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.certo: Your king goes to b5, on the black king's rank, with three squares between them.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.revela: The best is to bring the king to b5, on the black king's rank, with three squares between them.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.d2d3.1: The pawn advances before the king: your king, on a6, stays far from the key squares.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.d2d3.2: The black king goes to e5, one of the key squares, and also guards d5. Your king, on a6, is far from them.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.d2d4.1: The pawn advances two squares while your king is still far away, and is left unprotected.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.d2d4.2: The black king goes to e4 and attacks the pawn on d4, far from your king's protection.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6a5.1: Your king goes to a5, on the black king's rank, but leaves four squares between them: an even number.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6a5.2: The black king goes to e5 and leaves three squares between the kings after its move: Black has the lateral opposition.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6b6.1: Your king goes to b6, off the black king's rank, and does not win the lateral opposition.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6b6.2: The black king goes to e4 and, next move, can go to d3, in front of the pawn. Your king, on b6, is far from it.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6a7.1: Your king retreats to a7, off the black king's rank and farther from the key squares.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6a7.2: The black king goes to e4 and, next move, can go to d3, in front of the pawn. Your king, on a7, is far from it.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6b7.1: Your king retreats to b7, off the black king's rank and farther from the key squares.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.err.a6b7.2: The black king goes to e4 and, next move, can go to d3, in front of the pawn. Your king, on b7, is far from it.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.livre.fala: Keep playing with White and see how Black defends.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.fins.capturado: The black king captured the pawn.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.fins.repeticao: The black king always closes the way.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.fins.limite: The black king always closes the way.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l1: Your king went to b5, on the black king's rank, with three squares between them: c5, d5 and e5. An odd number, and you have just moved: the lateral opposition is yours.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l3: The black king goes to e4 and guards d4, one of the key squares.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l4: Your king goes to c4, a key square, facing the black king with only d4 between them: direct opposition, along the rank. With the king on c4, the pawn promotes whatever Black does.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l6: The black king retreats, and yours follows it. Only then does the pawn advance.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l7: Protected by the king, the pawn marches to the last rank and promotes.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l8: What if, after your first move, the black king goes to e5?
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l9: From e5, the black king guards d4 and e4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l10: Your king goes to c5 and faces it, with d5 between the kings: the direct opposition is yours.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l11: The black king advances to e4 and tries to guard d4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l12: You go to c4, facing it again, and reach a key square.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex1.l13: Back to the start: along a rank, count the squares as on a file. An odd number after your move, with your king on the way to the key squares, and the lateral opposition is yours.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.e1: Now the defence, from Black's side. The white king, on a6, wants c4, d4 or e4, the key squares; yours, on f7, closes the path with the same weapon: the opposition.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7e7.1: Your king goes to e7, off the white king's rank, and does not win the lateral opposition.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7e7.2: The white king goes to b5, one step from c4, a key square. From e7, your king cannot guard it in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7e8.1: Your king retreats to e8, off the white king's rank and far from the key squares c4, d4 and e4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7e8.2: The white king goes to b5, one step from c4, a key square. From e8, your king cannot guard it in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7f8.1: Your king retreats to f8, off the white king's rank and far from the key squares c4, d4 and e4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7f8.2: The white king goes to b5, one step from c4, a key square. From f8, your king cannot guard it in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7g6.1: Your king goes to g6: five squares, an odd number, but far from c4, d4 and e4. Counting is not enough: your king must arrive in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7g6.2: The white king goes to b5, one step from c4, a key square. From g6, your king cannot guard it in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7g7.1: Your king goes to g7, off the white king's rank and far from the key squares c4, d4 and e4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7g7.2: The white king goes to b5, one step from c4, a key square. From g7, your king cannot guard it in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7g8.1: Your king retreats to g8, off the white king's rank and far from the key squares c4, d4 and e4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7g8.2: The white king goes to b5, one step from c4, a key square. From g8, your king cannot guard it in time.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.p: Black to move. Think and suggest a move, or click {verResposta}
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.certo: Your king goes to e6, on the white king's rank, with three squares between them.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.revela: The best is to bring the king to e6, on the white king's rank, with three squares between them.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7f6.1: Your king goes to f6, on the white king's rank, but leaves four squares between them: an even number.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.err.f7f6.2: The white king goes to b6 and leaves three squares between the kings after its move: White has the lateral opposition.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.livre.fala: Keep playing with Black and see how White attacks.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.fins.coroa: The pawn promoted. Without the opposition, Black cannot hold.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.fins.limite: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.fins.repeticao: The white king controls the key squares: the pawn will promote.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.fins.capturado: The pawn fell: your king won the fight for the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.fins.afogado: Your king is stalemated: a draw, and the defence held.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.livre.volta: Let's go back to the starting position. Suggest another move or click {verResposta}
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.l1: Your king went to e6, on the white king's rank. Three squares between them, and you have just moved: the lateral opposition is yours.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.l2: The white king advances to b5, one step from c4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.l3: You answer on d5: only c5 between the kings, the direct opposition. From d5, your king guards c4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.l4: The white king goes to b4, heading for c4.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.l5: You follow to d4, facing it again. The white king reaches no key square: it is a draw.
rot.lateral.ideia.ex2.l6: Back to the start: in defence, the count is the same. An odd number after your move, with your king near the key squares, and the white king cannot get through. Next, an attack and a defence.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.1: Defence demonstration: now thinking from Black's side. The white pawn is on c2, and its key squares are b4, c4 and d4.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.2: Your king goes to b7, on the white king's rank. Between them lie c7, d7 and e7: three squares, and White is to move. The lateral opposition is yours.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.3: The white king comes down to e6, heading for the key squares.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.4: Your king comes down with it, to c6. Only d6 lies between the kings: the opposition is still yours.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.5: The white king comes down again, to e5, close to d4.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.6: Your king follows, to c5, next to b4, c4 and d4. The white king cannot reach the key squares, and it is a draw.
rot.lateral.demos.defesaLonge.ponte: Your turn: an attack and a defence against the machine. Before each move, count the squares between the kings, on the file or the rank: there may be three or five.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.enunciado: Play White and find the best move.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.fim: Your king took the lateral opposition, kept it until the direct opposition and entered d4, a key square: with the king there, the pawn promotes.
rot.lateral.pratica.defesa.enunciado: Play Black and find the best move.
rot.lateral.pratica.defesa.fim: Your king took the lateral opposition twice and reached c4, next to d4, before the white king.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.1: Attacking demonstration: pawn on d2, key squares c4, d4 and e4. Both kings are far from them, and White to move. Where does the white king take the opposition?
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.2: The white king goes to g7, on the black king's rank, with five squares between them, from b7 to f7, and Black to move. Five is odd: the lateral opposition belongs to White.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.3: The black king comes down diagonally to b6, heading for the key squares c4 and d4.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.4: The white king comes down with it, to f6: now c6, d6 and e6 lie between the kings, three squares. Both kings changed rank, and the count stays odd. Any other move draws.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.5: The black king comes down again, to c5, next to c4 and d4.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.6: The white king comes down to e5, face to face, with d5 between them. Advancing the pawn now would draw: the black king reaches it.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.7: The black king occupies c4, one of the key squares, and threatens to go to d3, attacking the pawn.
rot.lateral.demos.ataqueLonge.8: The white king enters e4, another key square, and guards d3: with the king there, the pawn promotes.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.err.e2e3: With the pawn advance, the win slips away: the key squares move up to d5, e5 and f5, and the black king, going to g5, reaches them before yours.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.err.e2e4: With the pawn advance, the win slips away: the key squares move up to d6, e6 and f6, and the black king, going to g5, is one step from f6.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.err.a7a6: On a6, your king is on the black king's rank, but with six squares between them: an even number. The black king goes to g5, towards f4, and the win slips away.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.err.a7b7: On b7, your king stays off the black king's rank and does not take the opposition: the black king goes to g5 and reaches the key squares first.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.err.a7a8: On a8, your king retreats away from the key squares d4, e4 and f4: the black king gets there first.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.err.a7b8: On b8, your king retreats away from the key squares d4, e4 and f4: the black king gets there first.

rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.v1.err.e2e3: The pawn advances with your king still far away: the key squares move up to d5, e5 and f5, and the black king, on g5, is already next to f5.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.v1.err.e2e4: The pawn advances to e4 with your king still far away: the black king goes to f4 and attacks the pawn.
rot.lateral.pratica.ataque.v2.err.c5c4: On c4, your king is on the black king's rank, but with two squares between them, d4 and e4: an even number. The black king goes to e3 and attacks the pawn.
